hook: If you've ended up doing most of the emotional labour in your friendships and you don't know how it happened — here's how it happened.
topic: Emotional labour imbalance as a confidence pattern outcome
body:
**If you're the one who always checks in, always makes the effort, always holds space — and you can't figure out how it became the default — I want to show you the mechanism.**

It didn't start because you were a pushover. It started because you're someone who learned, probably very early, that your role in relationships was to make things comfortable. To smooth things over. To need less and give more — because that's what kept things feeling safe.

So you did it well. You got good at it. And people calibrated to it.

What happens next is quiet and slow: you become the emotional infrastructure. The one who asks. The one who notices. The one who holds it together. And slowly, the relationship gets shaped around what you offer, not what you also need.

This isn't about blaming anyone. It's about understanding that the pattern started with a belief — the belief that needing less makes you more lovable. It doesn't. It makes you invisible.

Naming the pattern is the first step to changing it — link in bio for the full guide.
visual_direction: Luna seated, unhurried. On "more lovable" — slight pause and direct eye contact to let the line land. Warm but clear tone throughout.
text_overlay: "need less, give more" — shown as the belief that drives the pattern
caption_hook: If you're always the one who checks in, always holds space — here's how that became the default.
